message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.46","text":"Thus the voices that slander the God who created heaven are invalidated both by the opposing voices alongside them and by creation’s refutation; for they were not written by a prophetic hand, and consequently they also appear opposed to the hand of the God who created all things. And Simon said, “How can you demonstrate this?”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"αἱ τοῦ τὸν οὐρανὸν κτίσαντος θεοῦ διάβολοι φωναὶ","chosen":"the voices that slander the God who created heaven","rationale":"διάβολοι characterizes the voices as slanderous, while the genitive is understood objectively: their slander is directed against God."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῶν σὺν αὐταῖς ἐναντίων φωνῶν","chosen":"by the opposing voices alongside them","rationale":"This preserves both the opposition and the claim that the contrary voices occur together with the slanderous ones."},{"source_quote":"τῇ τοῦ τὰ πάντα κτίσαντος θεοῦ χειρὶ ἐναντίαι","chosen":"opposed to the hand of the God who created all things","rationale":"The repeated image of a writing hand is retained rather than reduced to a general reference to divine action."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.47","text":"And Peter said, “The law of God was given, unwritten, to seventy wise men to be handed down, so that it could be administered through succession. But after Moses’ taking up, it was written by someone, though certainly not by Moses; for in the law itself it is written, ‘And Moses died, and they buried him near the house of Phogor, and no one knows his burial place to this day.’ Was it possible for Moses, after dying, to write, ‘Moses died’? For in the period after Moses—perhaps some five hundred years or even more—it is found lying in the demolished temple; and after roughly another five hundred years it is carried away and, in the time of Nebuchadnezzar, is thus burned and perishes. And yet, although written after Moses and repeatedly lost, this law too acknowledged Moses’ foreknowledge: because he foresaw its disappearance, he did not write it. Those who wrote it, however, were exposed as ignorant by their failure to foreknow its disappearance, and so were not prophets.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἀγράφως ἐδόθη παραδίδοσθαι","chosen":"was given, unwritten, ... to be handed down","rationale":"ἀγράφως indicates oral rather than written delivery, while the passive infinitive expresses continued transmission."},{"source_quote":"ἵνα τῇ διαδοχῇ πολιτεύεσθαι δύνηται","chosen":"so that it could be administered through succession","rationale":"The middle-passive πολιτεύεσθαι can describe the law’s administration or its regulation of communal life; the chosen wording keeps the law as the grammatical subject."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ δὲ τὴν Μωϋσέως ἀνάληψιν","chosen":"after Moses’ taking up","rationale":"ἀνάληψις is rendered transparently without replacing the author’s expression with an explicit reference to death."},{"source_quote":"ἐν τῷ καθαιρισθέντι ναῷ","chosen":"in the demolished temple","rationale":"The uncommon printed form καθαιρισθέντι is understood in the destructive sense of dismantling or razing."},{"source_quote":"φέρεται","chosen":"it is carried away","rationale":"The passive of φέρω is taken as a further event affecting the law, rather than as the impersonal expression “it is reported.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸν ἀφανισμὸν αὐτοῦ","chosen":"its disappearance","rationale":"The masculine pronoun refers naturally to the law; ἀφανισμός here denotes its loss or removal from sight."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καθαιρισθέντι","issue":"The image-checked edition prints this uncommon form. It is interpreted here as a late or regularized formation with the sense “demolished” or “dismantled”; no alteration of the supplied reading has been made.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.48","text":"And Simon said, “Since, as you said, the things concerning God can be understood by comparison with creation, how is it possible to recognize the remaining things in the law, which derive from Moses’ tradition, are in fact true, and are mixed with false things?” And Peter said, “A certain passage in the written law, by God’s providence, was recalled without error, so as to show clearly which of the things written are true and which are false.” And Simon said, “What is it? Disclose it to us.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐκ τῆς πρὸς τὴν κτίσιν παραβολῆς","chosen":"by comparison with creation","rationale":"παραβολή here denotes comparison or setting one thing alongside another, not necessarily a narrative parable."},{"source_quote":"ἀληθῆ τυγχάνοντα","chosen":"are in fact true","rationale":"τυγχάνω with the participle emphasizes their actual state rather than chance."},{"source_quote":"Περικοπή τις","chosen":"A certain passage","rationale":"περικοπή denotes a bounded section or passage of text."},{"source_quote":"ἄπταιστος ἐπεμνημονεύθη","chosen":"was recalled without error","rationale":"ἐπιμνημονεύω concerns remembering or mentioning, while ἄπταιστος marks the passage as free from error; “recalled” retains that wording without claiming an unattested act of textual restoration."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τοῖς ψευδέσιν. μεμιγμένα","issue":"The printed period interrupts a single grammatical phrase, since μεμιγμένα agrees with the preceding neuter plural subject and takes τοῖς ψευδέσιν as its complement. The translation treats the period as an editorial punctuation anomaly rather than as a sentence boundary.","proposed_reading":"τοῖς ψευδέσιν μεμιγμένα","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.49","text":"And Peter said, “I will tell you at once. Near the end of the first book of the law it is written, ‘A ruler will not cease from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until the one whose it is comes; and he is the expectation of nations.’ Therefore, if anyone can understand the one who has come after the ruler and leader from Judah ceased and who is destined to be awaited by nations, this person, from what has been fulfilled, the passage . . . . . to recognize as true the one who has come. Without being persuaded by the teaching, he will know which parts of the Scriptures are true and which are false.” And Simon said, “I understand that you mean your Jesus, as the very one prophesied by Scripture. Let it therefore be granted that this is so. Tell me, then, how he taught you to distinguish the Scriptures.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ","chosen":"from his thighs","rationale":"The bodily image is retained rather than replaced by an interpretive term such as “descendants.”"},{"source_quote":"ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ οὗ ἐστιν","chosen":"until the one whose it is comes","rationale":"The compressed relative expression is preserved. It may also be understood as “until the one to whom it belongs comes.”"},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν προσδοκᾶσθαι μέλλοντα","chosen":"who is destined to be awaited by nations","rationale":"μέλλω marks the future expectation, and the passive construction leaves the nations as those doing the awaiting."},{"source_quote":"ἀληθῆ τὸν ἐληλυθότα ἐπιγνῶναι","chosen":"to recognize as true the one who has come","rationale":"ἀληθῆ is attached predicatively to τὸν ἐληλυθότα, the nearest matching phrase. Because the printed gap disrupts the syntax, attachment to περικοπή—“to recognize the passage as true”—remains a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"οὐ τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ πειθόμενος γνώσεται","chosen":"Without being persuaded by the teaching, he will know","rationale":"The negated participle is taken as modifying the manner in which he will know, contrasting recognition from fulfilled events with persuasion by teaching."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οὗτος τὴν περικοπὴν ἐκ τῶν ἀποτελεσθέντων . . . . . ἀληθῆ τὸν ἐληλυθότα ἐπιγνῶναι","issue":"The selected edition contains a clearly printed five-dot lacuna that interrupts the construction and leaves the surviving accusatives and infinitive without a complete governing syntax. The same five dots have been retained in the English, and no missing wording has been restored.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.50","text":"And Peter said, “As evidence that the true things are mixed with the false, I recall that somewhere, while reproaching the Sadducees, he said, ‘This is why you go astray: you do not know the true things in the Scriptures, and because of this you are ignorant of the power of God.’ Now if he implied that they were ignorant of the true things in the Scriptures, it is plain that false ones also exist. Moreover, by saying, ‘Become approved money changers,’ he indicated that there are both genuine and counterfeit sayings. And by saying, ‘Why do you not understand what is reasonable in the Scriptures?’ he makes the understanding of the person who exercises sound judgment by personal choice more secure.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὰ ἀληθῆ τῶν γραφῶν","chosen":"the true things in the Scriptures","rationale":"The partitive expression distinguishes true contents within the writings rather than treating “the Scriptures” collectively as the direct object of knowing."},{"source_quote":"γίνεσθε τραπεζῖται δόκιμοι","chosen":"Become approved money changers","rationale":"τραπεζῖται retains the monetary image, while δόκιμοι describes persons proven competent or approved in testing what they receive."},{"source_quote":"δοκίμων καὶ κιβδήλων λόγων","chosen":"genuine and counterfeit sayings","rationale":"The contrast extends the coin-testing image: δόκιμος is genuine or approved, whereas κίβδηλος is adulterated or counterfeit."},{"source_quote":"τὸ εὔλογον τῶν γραφῶν","chosen":"what is reasonable in the Scriptures","rationale":"The substantival adjective may denote the reasonable content, meaning, or portion of the writings; the chosen wording leaves those closely related possibilities open."},{"source_quote":"βεβαιότερον τοῦ αὐθαιρέτως εὐγνωμονοῦντος τίθησιν τὸν νοῦν","chosen":"he makes the understanding of the person who exercises sound judgment by personal choice more secure","rationale":"The genitive is taken possessively with τὸν νοῦν. Alternatively, it can be construed comparatively: “he establishes understanding more firmly than one who judges soundly on his own authority.”"}],"source_issues":[]}]}
